title: Minimum Path Cost in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid with distinct integers from 0 to m * n - 1, you can move to any cell in the next row.
statement: Given an m x n grid with distinct integers from 0 to m * n - 1, you can move to any cell in the next row. Each move has a cost defined in a 2D array. The cost of a path includes the sum of cell values and move costs. Find the minimum cost path from any cell in the first row to any cell in the last row, ignoring the move cost in the last row.
constraints: Start in any first-row cell and choose one cell in each following row.
Moving from a cell with value v to next-row column c costs move_cost[v][c].
Total cost includes every visited cell value plus every inter-row move cost.
hints: Dynamic programming needs only the cheapest cost ending at each column of the current row.
To enter next cell value at column c, try every previous column and add its path cost plus move_cost[previous_value][c].
Add the new cell value to the best transition, repeat rows, and return the minimum final cost.
Every path has one predecessor in the prior row; minimizing all such transitions preserves the cheapest path to each state.
editorial: Every path has one predecessor in the prior row; minimizing all such transitions preserves the cheapest path to each state.

tests.explanation: The cheapest complete top-to-bottom path costs seventeen.
With free moves, choosing values zero then two costs two.
